newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Four Russian journalists released in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Four Russian journalists released in Chechnya.

text.p: Four Russian journalists who were kidnapped and taken hostage in Chechnya over three months ago have been released, Russian news agencies reported on Friday.
Three of the journalists are from Radio Russia and the fourth, Nikolai Zagnoiko, is a correspondent for Itar-Tass news agency.
"All four are alive and in good health," Zagnoiko told Tass. "We are safe and will soon be in Moscow."
Magomed Toboyev, a security official from the neighbouring ethnic region of Dagestan who was closely involved in efforts to free the hostages, told Tass no ranson had been paid.

He said they were freed "as a result of a complicated operation based on personal contacts, with the assistance of official Chechen structures and Chechnya and Dagestan police as well as federal services".

Tass said a senior Russian security official, Boris Berezovsky, who had secured the release of another group of Russian journalists earlier this year, had flown to Dagestan and would escort the freed journalists to Moscow.
Kidnapping for ransom has become a profitable business in Chechnya in Russia's north Caucasus region.
Chechnya was heavily damaged in 21 months of fighting between separatists and Russian troops trying to quell an independence drive. Nearly every man has a weapon and jobs are scarce.

Fighting ended last August and peace was secured by a deal signed in Moscow last week. Freeing of hostages, especially Russian journalists, has become a burning issue for Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov, who has to prove his grip on power.
Three other journalists -- a crew from the commercial NTV television kidnapped a month ago -- are still being held in Chechnya.
